findings.claim: The source mapping drops `ref`. claude 2.1.300 compares the add argument with the whole settings entry: a github entry with ref main refuses `scaccogatto/okf-skills` and accepts `scaccogatto/okf-skills#main`, and a git entry with ref main refuses the bare URL and accepts `URL#main`. As planned (repo for github, url for git), any entry that pins a ref still fails with the operator's exact error. The mapping must append `#ref` when the entry has one, and r1 must cover entries with a ref.

The plan picks between passing a source and refusing it by the source kind alone, but other fields also have to match. A github entry with `path` (where marketplace.json lives) refuses the bare repo, and `marketplace add` has no option that carries `path`. Under the plan, that entry gets the repo string, the add fails with claude's error, and the install never reaches the PluginError that names the settings file. The plan must decide pass or refuse from the entry's fields (kind plus ref, path, and any other field it cannot carry, such as url headers or git path), and r2 should name a passable kind that carries an unpassable field.

The plan says kmctl reads 'the managed settings' but does not name the files, and it does not say where the operator's entry lives. claude 2.1.300 reads managed settings from /etc/claude-code (Linux) or /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode (macOS): managed-settings.json plus the drop-in folder managed-settings.d/, and also from MDM and server-managed policy. If the operator's entry is in a drop-in file, an MDM profile or remote policy, the fix as written does not fix the operator's install. The plan must name the paths it reads (including managed-settings.d/*.json), say what happens for sources kmctl cannot read, and confirm the operator's entry is in a file it reads.

Inside the managed files the plan takes the first scaccogatto entry, but claude takes the last: it reads managed-settings.json, then managed-settings.d/*.json in sorted name order, and each later file's entry replaces the earlier one. With entries in two managed files kmctl would pass the argument for the entry claude does not compare against, and the add fails with the operator's error.

The plan assumes the entry's own field (url[#ref] for git, url for url) is an add argument claude reads back as the same entry. It is not always. claude 2.1.300 parses the add string itself (Jme): an https URL is git only if it ends in .git or has /_git/; on github and other known hosts an owner/repo URL gets .git appended; any other https URL becomes a url source; ssh:// URLs are rejected. A git entry such as https://github.com/scaccogatto/okf-skills (no .git) therefore gives a source with a different url, and a git entry on a self-hosted host without .git gives a url source. Both fail the full-equality check. Probed in an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/HOME/XDG_DATA_HOME: user entry {git, https://github.com/scaccogatto/okf-skills}, `claude plugin marketplace add https://github.com/scaccogatto/okf-skills --scope project` fails with the operator's exact message. kmctl would then show the error that tells the operator to "add it from the source that entry lists", which kmctl just did. The plan should treat such an entry as one with no matching add argument (stop with the PluginError before claude runs) or narrow which git and url entries it accepts. The r1 and r3 tests check only the string kmctl builds, so they would pass while the real add fails; r3 (or a new row) should cover a git entry without .git.

an entry whose source is missing, not a dict, or lacks its repo/url/path field is treated as live, but claude 2.1.300 ignores it; kmctl then refuses an install claude would allow, or runs `marketplace add None`
the dot-file case in test_okf_source_managed_wins cannot fail, because .99-hidden.json sorts before 10-a.json and would lose even if kmctl read it
_isolated_home reads os through __import__("os") instead of a normal import

entries.change: An entry without a source object, a string kind, or a string location for its kind is ignored as claude ignores it, so the default add or an earlier good entry is used and no add of None happens.
Broken entries (empty, string source, no repo, no kind) fall back to the default or an earlier entry; the dot-file check now fails if a dot-file is read; os is imported normally.

findings.claim: a malformed scaccogatto entry was treated as live when claude ignores it
the dot-file check in the r2 test could not fail
use a plain import os in _isolated_home
